summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of kidney transplant, and multiple comorbidities was admitted due to a new vesicular rash concerning for varicella infection. She had recent exposure to her father with shingles and no prior vaccination or immunity. Diagnosis was confirmed by positive varicella direct antigen test. She was treated with seven days of IV acyclovir and IV fluids to protect her renal function, with stable creatinine throughout. The rash progressed to crusting with no new lesions, and she was no longer infectious at discharge. Immunosuppressive therapy was adjusted temporarily, with Cellcept halved and later restored. Glycemic control improved with ongoing insulin pump management. She remained afebrile with no complications such as pneumonia or encephalitis. She was discharged home on her baseline medications with follow-up planned for liver and kidney function.
